title: Composition of derived direct images
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. Let $X\xrightarrow f Y\xrightarrow g Z$ be morphisms of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the finite derived direct images of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. For the integral formula in that definition, specify its functorial realization as follows: form the strict reduction tower on a K-flat representative as in [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], restrict each term to the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], apply ordinary total derived direct image on the strict tower category, and then total derived inverse limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. This chooses a functorial derived-limit realization; an arbitrary Roos triangle alone is not the meaning of the integral functor here.

There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$c_{g,f}:R(gf)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*Rf_*$$
with the following domains and codomains:
1. At finite level, on all of $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$, valued in $D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$.
2. Integrally, on the full subcategory of $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] consisting of $K$ with $Rf_*K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, valued in the ambient $D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$.
3. Rationally [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], on the scalar localization of the full subcategory in (2) whose objects also satisfy $R(gf)_*K\in D^b_c(Z,\mathcal O_E)$, valued in $D^b_c(Z,E)$.
4. In the common-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], on pairs $(E,K)$ with $K$ in (3), valued in $D^b_c(Z,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$. The domain is the full common-stage subcategory; the conditions are preserved on extending the coefficient field.
5. On the small etale site with any commutative ring $A$, on all of the ordinary unbounded $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, valued in $D(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$.

Under the canonical identity identifications the comparison is the identity if either map is an identity. For $h:Z\to W$, the two composites from $R(hgf)_*K$ to $Rh_*Rg_*Rf_*K$ agree whenever all intermediate integral applications are defined (and, at the rational and common stages, all displayed values are bounded constructible). It respects transport along automorphisms of the diagram; direct image along $\sigma$ identifies with inverse image along $\sigma^{-1}$.

proof.text: Work with the small site models in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. For finite constant coefficients, and for arbitrary constant commutative coefficients on the small etale site, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to obtain the canonical natural isomorphism $\kappa_{g,f}:R(gf)_*\cong Rg_*Rf_*$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. These are the finite functors of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. For later use put $F_u=Ru_*^{\wedge}$, ordinary total derived module direct image along the completed coefficient sheaves of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Its structural ring map is induced from the finite constant coefficient maps of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and their inverse limit. The same general ringed-topos lemma gives $\kappa_{g,f}:F_{gf}\cong F_gF_f$. No assertion that inverse image commutes with the completed coefficient limit is needed.

source.place: Finite paragraph; general completed-module comparison; Stacks Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition

proof.text:
Here is the coherence check for the normalized ordinary comparisons, including completed-ring and tower topoi. Take a K-injective representative $I$ and resolutions $j:f_*I\to J$ and $k:g_*J\to H$ with $J,H$ K-injective, using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] says that $g_*j$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $k\,g_*j:g_*f_*I\to H$ is also a K-injective resolution. With this choice both triple comparisons are represented by
$$h_*g_*f_*I\xrightarrow{h_*g_*j}h_*g_*J\xrightarrow{h_*k}h_*H.$$
Changing a resolution gives the same class by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]: maps into a K-injective target in the derived category are exactly homotopy classes of chain maps. For an identity morphism choose the identity resolution of $I$. This proves the identity and associativity equations for $\kappa$, rather than taking them from an unstated extra clause of the composition lemma.

source.place: Finite paragraph, identity and associativity; normalized resolution argument

proof.text:
The reduction construction is a single strict-tower functor. On a K-flat complex $P$ with flat terms send $P$ to $T_E(P)=(\operatorname{Res}_n(P\otimes_R(A_{E,n})_U))_n$, with all quotient transitions from [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], where $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,U}$. Chain maps and chain homotopies tensor with the identity at every level, so commute with all transitions. A quasi-isomorphism of such representatives induces levelwise quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], clause (1). These are quasi-isomorphisms of tower complexes because exactness and cohomology are levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. The equivalence $W_R^{-1}\mathcal P_R\simeq D(R)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] therefore descends this functor to
$$T_E:D(R)\longrightarrow D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R))).$$
This uses localization of the whole strict tower, not only an inverse system of derived objects.

source.place: Integral paragraph: strict reduction functor; Stacks Tags 06YT, 06YY

proof.text:
Let $L_U=R\lim$ on the strict tower category [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Countable products of completed-ring modules on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are exact [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Apply [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] to $T_E(K)$. It identifies $L_UT_E(K)$ naturally with the functorial product-cone realization, and carries the strict quotient augmentation to the map with zero shifted-product component. Consequently the case $L=E$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] gives a specified natural isomorphism
$$\eta_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}L_UT_E(K)$$
for every derived-complete $K$. The normalization clause of the new comparison identifies this particular map; a general lift of $K\to\prod_nK_n$ would not suffice.

source.place: Integral paragraph: completion isomorphism and its functorial normalization; Stacks Tag 0941

proof.text: For $u:U\to V$ and coefficient restriction $r_{U,n},r_{V,n}$, the two ringed-topos composites obtained by first pushing forward or first restricting coefficients have the same underived module direct image. Since $r_{U,n},r_{V,n}$ are exact [lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact], applying [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to both composites gives $F_u r_{U,n}\cong r_{V,n}Ru_{*,n}$. The evaluation isomorphisms of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] therefore identify each term of $RF_u^{\operatorname{Tow}}T_E(K)$ with $\operatorname{Res}_nRu_{*,n}(K\otimes^L A_{E,n})$. For every quotient $A_{E,m}\to A_{E,n}$ the two identifications are those of the same composite coefficient ring map; the associativity of $\kappa$ proved in step 2 makes the transition identifications commute. Thus these are exactly the transitions prescribed by [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

source.place: Integral paragraph: coefficient restriction and evaluation of the strict pushforward tower

proof.text:
Write $\mathcal R_u(K)=L_VRF_u^{\operatorname{Tow}}T_E(K)$ for the integral realization in the statement. The natural comparison $a_{u,T}:F_uL_U(T)\cong L_VRF_u^{\operatorname{Tow}}(T)$ in [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] gives
$$b_u(K)=a_{u,T_E(K)}\circ F_u(\eta_K):F_uK\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal R_uK.$$
It is natural on derived-complete inputs. Step 5 identifies its target with the specified finite-level formula. For $K$ in clause (2), both $K$ and $\mathcal R_fK$ are derived complete by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Hence $b_f(K)$, $b_{gf}(K)$ and $b_g(\mathcal R_fK)$ are all defined and invertible; no constructibility of $\mathcal R_{gf}K$ is needed here.

source.place: Integral paragraph: identify the specified direct image with ordinary completed-module direct image

proof.text:
Define the integral comparison by
$$c_{g,f,K}=b_g(\mathcal R_fK)\circ F_g(b_f(K))\circ\kappa_{g,f,K}\circ b_{gf}(K)^{-1}.$$
Each factor is a natural isomorphism, so this proves clause (2). For the identity morphism, $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{id}}K=L_UT_E(K)$ with identity identification $\eta_K^{-1}$; equivalently use $b_{\mathrm{id}}^{-1}$ under the canonical ordinary identity identification. Substitute this in the formula. If $f=\mathrm{id}$, the factors $F_g(\eta_K)$ and the corresponding identification of the input cancel; if $g=\mathrm{id}$, the factors $\eta_{\mathcal R_fK}$ cancel. In both cases the remaining ordinary comparison is the identity of step 2. All constructions are $\mathcal O_E$-linear: multiplication by a constant section commutes with tensor, quotient maps, resolutions and their comparison maps.

source.place: Integral paragraph: explicit compositor, naturality, identity, and coefficient linearity

proof.text:
For three maps, expand both composites using the formula of step 7. The hypotheses ensure that every integral input to a $b$ is derived complete; an ordinary intermediate $F_uK$ is isomorphic through $b_u$ to the displayed complete intermediate, so is complete as well. Naturality of $b_h$ moves $b_g$ through it, and naturality of $\kappa_{h,g}$ moves $b_f$ through that comparison. Cancel each adjacent inverse pair. Both expressions become
$$b_h(\mathcal R_g\mathcal R_fK)\,F_h(b_g(\mathcal R_fK))\,F_hF_g(b_f(K))\,\kappa^{(3)}\,b_{hgf}(K)^{-1},$$
where the two ordinary choices of $\kappa^{(3)}:F_{hgf}K\to F_hF_gF_fK$ agree by step 2. This proves associativity with the specified units. It makes no uniqueness claim about maps between Roos triangles.

source.place: Integral paragraph: cancellation proof of triple coherence

proof.text: On the full integral subcategory in clause (3), $\mathcal R_fK$ and $\mathcal R_{gf}K$ are bounded constructible, and step 7 places $\mathcal R_g\mathcal R_fK$ in the same output category. In [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] objects are unchanged and each Hom is tensored with $E$. Extend all integral functor maps and comparison components $\mathcal O_E$-linearly. For a pure tensor $u\otimes a$ naturality is the integral equation multiplied by $a$; sums give every morphism. Images of inverse components remain inverses, and the identity and associativity equations remain equalities. This proves clause (3), with its necessary output condition.

For coefficient extension $E\subset L$, first establish an ordinary integral basis from existing arithmetic statements. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $\mathcal O_E$ is a DVR with fraction field $E$, hence a PID. It is Noetherian and normal by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. The extension $L/E$ is separable: characteristic zero makes each irreducible polynomial coprime to its derivative. By [lem-sfb-padic-integers-integral-closure] and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite], $\mathcal O_L$ is a finite $\mathcal O_E$-module. It is torsion-free as a submodule of the field $L$. Thus [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] supplies an integral basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$. This is also an $E$-basis of $L$: multiply any element of $L$, or the finitely many coefficients of a putative relation, by a sufficiently large power of $\ell$ to put it in the integral rings. Spanning and independence reduce to those of the integral basis, so $d=[L:E]$.

source.place: Tag 032L, lemma-Noetherian-normal-domain-finite-separable-extension; blueprint algebraically closed paragraph: integral basis

proof.text:
The same basis gives completed coefficient identifications on every scheme. The DVR factorization in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] gives $t=uv^e$, $e\geq1$, for $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_L$; positivity follows from $|t|_L<1$. The sequences of ideals $(t^n)\mathcal O_L=(v^{en})$ and $(v^m)$ are cofinal. Restriction to the indices $en$ gives an isomorphism of inverse limits: a compatible sequence at those indices determines its $m$th component by reducing any term with $en\geq m$, independently of the choice. Modulo $t^n$, the basis identifies $\mathcal O_L/t^n\mathcal O_L$ with $(\mathcal O_E/t^n)^d$. These inverse maps sheafify to inverse maps of constant module sheaves; a finite tuple of locally constant sections is locally a constant tuple after a common refinement. Taking inverse limits, coordinate by coordinate, yields
$$S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}\cong (\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W})^{\oplus d}=R_W^{\oplus d}$$
with formula $(x_i)\mapsto\sum_i e_ix_i$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. The structural maps of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] send each constant $e_i$ to itself, so these bases are compatible on the entire scheme diagram. Product bases for successive coefficient extensions give the tensor associator by multiplication of their constant basis elements.

source.place: Algebraically closed paragraph: finite coefficient basis, cofinal uniformizer powers, and compatible completed coefficient maps

proof.text:
Write $T_W=S_W\otimes_{R_W}-$ and $U_W$ for coefficient restriction. Step 11 gives $S_W=R_W^{\oplus d}$ on the whole scheme diagram. Both $T_W,U_W$ are exact, and $U_W$ detects quasi-isomorphisms by unchanged kernels and sheafified cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The balanced formula $h\mapsto(x\mapsto h(1\otimes x))$, with inverse $a\mapsto(s\otimes x\mapsto sa(x))$, gives $T_W\dashv U_W$ on modules [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and on complexes, respecting homotopies. If $J$ is K-injective over $S_W$, then $U_WJ$ is K-injective: an acyclic $B$ has acyclic $T_WB$, so the same adjunction kills every map $B\to U_WJ$ up to homotopy. Resolve the target by such a $J$ [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; the homotopy-to-derived bijection [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] therefore gives $T_W\dashv U_W$ on unbounded derived categories.
The equal ringed-topos composites give $U_VF^L_u\cong F^E_uU_U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Define $\beta_u:T_VF^E_uK\to F^L_uT_UK$ as the adjoint of $F^E_u(K\to U_UT_UK)$ under this comparison. After restriction, its map on each basis summand is the identity comparison induced by $x\mapsto e_i\otimes x$. Finite sums of K-injective resolutions are K-injective, so an additive derived functor commutes with these sums. Hence $U_V\beta_u$ is an isomorphism, and conservativity makes $\beta_u$ an isomorphism for all unbounded inputs.

source.place: Algebraically closed paragraph: finite-free ordinary scalar/direct-image comparison

proof.text:
Check equations for $\beta$ using the adjunction of step 12, which detects equality of the original $S$-linear derived maps. The adjuncts of the two scheme-composition routes are the same map obtained by applying $F_gF_f$ to $K\to U_UT_UK$ and then the ordinary comparison $\kappa$. This follows from naturality of the unit and step 2's coherence for the ringed-topos composites involving restriction. For $E\subset L\subset M$, take the successive adjunctions: their units send $x$ to $1\otimes(1\otimes x)$, identified with $1\otimes x$ by $s'\otimes(s\otimes x)\mapsto(s's)\otimes x$. Thus the coefficient tower and identity equations also hold. This uses adjunction, not faithfulness of derived restriction.
On complete objects use the specified natural $\chi_{L/E}:S_W\otimes^L_{R_W}K\cong T_{L/E}K$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Transport $\beta_u$ through $\chi$ and $b$ to obtain $\theta_u:T_{L/E}\mathcal R_{u,E}\cong\mathcal R_{u,L}T_{L/E}$ wherever integral outputs are constructible. Its factors are $\chi_V^{-1}$, $S_V\otimes b_{u,E}^{-1}$, $\beta_u$, $F^L_u(\chi_U)$, and $b_{u,L}$. Naturality cancels all intermediate inverse pairs in the composition equations as in step 8. The resulting coefficient associators are those of [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition].

source.place: Algebraically closed paragraph: comparison maps and coefficient coherence

proof.text: If $K$ is in the domain of clause (3), [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible] puts $T_{L/E}K$, $T_{L/E}\mathcal R_fK$, and $T_{L/E}\mathcal R_{gf}K$ in the corresponding integral constructible categories. The isomorphisms $\theta_f$ and $\theta_{gf}$ identify the latter two with the required direct images after extension. This proves preservation of the domain conditions. Rationalize $\theta$ as in step 9. By [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] a common-stage arrow is represented by a map $u$ over one finite extension $L$. Apply rational naturality at $L$ and use $\theta$ to identify its source and target; the equation gives naturality for the class of $u$. If two representatives agree over $M$, the coefficient tower equation in step 13 gives equal resulting classes over $M$. Composition, identity and triple coherence are equations at one common finite field, and therefore remain equations in the directed colimit. This proves clause (4).

source.place: Algebraically closed paragraph: full common-stage subcategory, descent, and naturality

proof.text: For a scheme isomorphism $\sigma$, [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] identifies the sheaf topoi by equivalences, and identifies constant coefficient maps compatibly with every quotient. Equivalences preserve all limits, so this also identifies the completed coefficient sheaves. Direct image along $\sigma$ is therefore inverse image along $\sigma^{-1}$ and is exact on their module categories. It may be derived using identity resolutions; the strict quotient towers and their completion units are carried along the same equivalences. The ordinary etale assertion follows in the same way by relabelling the objects of the small etale sites. For a commuting automorphism of $X\to Y\to Z$, the two routes transporting $c_{g,f}$ are reassociations of this same composite of direct images. Steps 2 and 8 make them equal. Rationalization and common-stage passage preserve this equality as in steps 9 and 14.

Replaced the long hidden cone comparison by one smaller strict-Roos comparison node. Reused the existing arithmetic integral-closure and DVR freeness nodes to obtain a diagram-wide completed coefficient basis; discarded a provisional overlapping basis node. Used the existing K-flat localization theorem for strict-tower descent. Gave normalized ordinary coherence, explicit conjugation, scalar comparison factors and common-stage naturality. tool_uses.why: General unbounded ringed-topos comparison, also for coefficient restriction; the unit does not provide this general result.
Uniqueness up to homotopy for normalized K-injective comparisons, without a bounded-below hypothesis.
Strict total derived inverse limit rather than a nonfunctorial choice of a Roos triangle.
Generic exactness of tower evaluation used only to check quasi-isomorphisms of strict towers.
Generic localization equivalence for K-flat flat-term representatives, used to descend one strict tower functor.
Identifies the actual valuation ring as the arithmetic integral closure, without identifying condensed and completed sheaf categories.
Arithmetic DVR and uniformizer factorization for coefficient fields, used to construct compatible bases and compare the two adic indices.
Generic site-equivalence theorem supplies exact transport along a scheme isomorphism.

Statement: the inherited corrected statement is kept verbatim and matches the blueprint (master order 1470 and main-20261015 order 1829 have identical statements). The integral realization only makes the derived-limit choice explicit. The added R(gf)_*K in D^b_c condition in (3)-(4) is necessary, not a weakening: I checked the counterexample of a countable disjoint union of points mapping to the point. Steps 1-15: each step's cited statements say what the step uses. Step 2: both triple κ routes are h_*k∘h_*g_*j. Step 3: descent goes through the W^{-1}P_R≃D(R) equivalence. Step 4: the cone model of def-weil-integral-scalar-extension with L=E is exactly C(T_E P), and both use the zero-shift augmentation. Steps 6 and 8: every b is applied only to derived-complete inputs. Step 10: the DVR→PID→Noetherian normal chain, separability in characteristic 0, integral closure, finiteness and freeness all have their hypotheses. Step 11: t=uv^e and the cofinality are correct. Steps 12-13: β is defined by adjunction, U is conservative, and θ has five factors; lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition's own proof defines its associator by χ-conjugation, so the tower equation transports. Step 14: domain preservation uses integral-scalar-extension-constructible. Step 15: transport uses the iso-inverse-image node. New node lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison: it is true. Exact products make C invert quasi-isomorphisms; injective towers have surjective transitions by the Stacks 0941 proof (l.5067ff), so lim I→C(I) is a quasi-isomorphism; (γ,0) is a chain map because (1-s)γ=0.
